extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and organizations applying for NEA Research Grants in the Arts (U.S.-based arts researchers, evaluators, and project teams)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and review criteria for preparing and submitting an application to the NEA Research Grants in the Arts program (includes Research Grants and Research Labs tiers). Describes eligibility checks, panel review process, review criteria, required proposal components, eligible topic areas, and program expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and completeness check
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are checked for completeness and eligibility by NEA staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must meet the program's eligibility rules and submit complete applications; incomplete or ineligible submissions may be removed from further review at Stage 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory panel review (interdisciplinary panelists)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applications are reviewed in closed session by interdisciplinary research and evaluation advisory panelists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels are composed of a diverse group of arts-research experts, other individuals, and at least one knowledgeable layperson; review is conducted in closed session and informs panel recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel recommendation formation
rubrics_metrics.description: The panel recommends the projects to be supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panelists evaluate applications against the review criteria and produce recommendations that are forwarded to NEA staff for reconciliation with available funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff reconciliation with available funds
rubrics_metrics.description: NEA staff reconciles panel recommendations with available funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff may adjust recommendations based on budgetary constraints and program priorities before forwarding to the National Council on the Arts.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Council on the Arts review
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations are forwarded to the National Council on the Arts and reviewed in an open public session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council reviews the recommended projects and makes recommendations to the NEA Chair; this is a public step in the decision process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final decision authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The NEA Chair reviews the recommendations and makes the final decision on all grant awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final funding decisions rest with the NEA Chair after panel, staff, and Council reviews; applicants should understand multi-stage decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance of the research question
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance of the research question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess whether the study addresses an important problem or question about the value/impact of the arts and whether findings would matter to the field, policy, practice, or the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical or methodological contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Theoretical or methodological contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should demonstrate how the project advances theory or methods in arts research (e.g., novel conceptual framing, new measurement approaches, or methodological innovation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of research design
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of research design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should present clear research design elements (explicit hypotheses or research questions, appropriate design choice, sample/population specification, and alignment between questions and methods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor of methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Rigor of methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong methodological rigor is required; reviewers evaluate robustness, validity, reliability, and appropriateness of analytic approaches. Quantitative, qualitative, and mixed methods are accepted if rigorous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capability of the research team
rubrics_metrics.description: Capability of research team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider investigators' qualifications, prior experience, and capacity to carry out the proposed research (including institutional support and collaborators).

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential to advance knowledge in the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential to advance knowledge in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should have clear contributions to scholarship, advance understanding of the arts' value/impact, or fill notable knowledge gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential to inform arts policy and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential to inform arts policy/practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers value research that can influence policy, improve arts practice, or provide actionable evidence for stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and confidentiality standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The NEA seeks to make its review process transparent while protecting the confidentiality of applicants, panelists, staff, and Council members; the names of applicants are kept confidential except for those who receive grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should expect a balance of transparency and confidentiality; only awardees' names are publicly disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open data and reproducibility encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: Open data and reproducibility encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEA values public-facing research and encourages practices that support data sharing and reproducibility where appropriate, which may strengthen review assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-facing research valued
rubrics_metrics.description: Public-facing research valued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that engage public audiences, produce accessible outputs, or have clear dissemination strategies for non-academic stakeholders are favorably regarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible research topic areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Research topics the program supports: economic impact of the arts; cognitive/educational benefits; health and wellbeing benefits; community development; creative careers and labor markets; audience research; arts and technology; cross-domain effects of arts engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should align with one or more of these eligible areas; proposals outside these themes may be less competitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical required proposal components
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical grant components: research design (clear hypothesis or research questions), theoretical framework, methodology, sample/population, data collection plan, analysis plan, dissemination plan, budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should provide detailed, coherent plans for each component; omissions or vague plans weaken competitiveness. Include explicit dissemination and budget justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award tiers and budget expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Award tiers: Research Grants in the Arts ($20,000 - $100,000) and Research Labs ($100,000 - $300,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should request funding consistent with proposed scope and appropriate tier; budget must align with project activities and NEA limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Competition is described as 'extremely rigorous.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should expect strong competition and prepare high-quality, methodologically rigorous, and well-justified proposals to be competitive.
